answer: Lock each identity's claim to a work history that accrues one entry per epoch, capped and not transferable. An auditor drawn from a rotating pool checks a random sample against those entries. A hundred clones spun in one afternoon carry a hundred empty histories, so every one fails the cap check before a payout is computed. There is no haven in that tundra of blank records. The kernel of the design is time, which a forger cannot copy.
